title: Release of Bicentenaria, a New Potato Cultivar for Processing in Peru
content: The origin and genealogy of "Bicentenaria", its development, agronomic characteristics, and performance within different environments are described. "Bicentenaria" was developed by Universidad Nacional Jose Faustino Sanchez Carrion (Peru) from a cross between three commercial cultivars for processing of tetraploid Solanum tuberosum cultivars: Reiche (Peru), Diacol Capiro (Colombia) and Atlantic (USA). The potato cultivar "Bicentenaria" (Register No. 001-2021-DELYC-SENASA) exhibits early maturity, competitive productivity, and adaptation capacity throughout the central coast of Peru with an average yield of 44.8 t ha-1, compared to the cultivars Canchan INIA (37.2 t ha-1) and Diacol Capiro (32.5 t ha-1). Its short vegetative period, high yields and solids content, combined with an appropriate tuber type make it a suitable potato for processing into products like French fries and chips.
